## Design

### 2026-11-08: I had started the week with a quite set idea of what i wanted to achieve - a  decoder for z scale trains and somehow as I was thinking over this project over the past few weeks as it came to me I was

**2.75h**

I had started the week with a quite set idea of what i wanted to achieve - a  decoder for z scale trains and somehow as I was thinking over this project over the past few weeks as it came to me I was quite certain I knew how to do it - Basically I wanted to add my signal on top of the 10 V DC already on my dreach and then have some basic analog circuitry to decode. It was for this reason I once again started my project in KICad so I could simulate it later.

![Screenshot 2026-11-08 at 12.12.06](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/afB45WLTnSAsFqrMq92IoTER2dLA2UXI/729a5039eb622fa4d07d2e4bf309b753853a2667c75540665113d93d260765fe.png)

Being a bit lazy I started with with the easy parts first with some components that I took a while to select but another thing I failed to consider was how big they are since I had not really set my constraints yet.

It was then a good 2 hours into this that as I was doing research I read through how normal decoders work... and well yeah all that work I  just did was down the drain.

![Screenshot 2026-11-08 at 12.18.50](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/afB45WLTnSAsFqrMq92IoTER2dLA2UXI/5753507a44aaff365695cb79b869ea0df101fdb66d1cd8d4022ec59fdcce3d83.png)

The basis of how DCC decoders work led me down a rabbit hole - although this open source version exists it is far to big and over capable for what I need with just motor and led control.

luckily the DCC protocol is largely standardized just that z scale locomotives have a smaller voltage of 10V rather than 12 or higher. the basic principle is that data is sent as rapid square wave over the tack - or as the standardization page puts it

" The DCC signal is a bipolar square waveform, which contains digital information. Long pulses are zero and short pulses are ones. A Command Station sends approximately 8,000 bits per second. The frequency does vary between about 5kHz-9kHz depending on the information sent and the bit duration being near the nominal values and not the max or min values."

Since I also didn't  know what all this meant at first  I found a helpful page that better explained what this signal than actually looks like if you were to analyse it.

![Screenshot 2026-11-08 at 12.23.39](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/afB45WLTnSAsFqrMq92IoTER2dLA2UXI/a06877b517fe19c00e42ea4f2b1a1ff5ac66ceaec766f9f50c47ac1b207b4fb5.png)

### 2026-11-08: With my new knowledge in hand and seeing I did not need KICad anymore I switched to fusion and went searching for better sized components - it is always quite annoying to upload them but most of this

**3.08h**

With my new knowledge in hand and seeing I did not need KICad anymore I switched to fusion and went searching for better sized components - it is always quite annoying to upload them but most of this time was just looking for a component then getting it into fusion and understanding from the data sheets how to hook it up

I also had to take the time to find new packages for everything since in my further research I decided i want this board to be small enough to fit on some standard train carriages so that limited me to about  12x7.5mm

[Timelapse](https://lookout.hackclub.com/api/media/8c427022-5c45-42d4-946a-a716ea26d2e9/video.mp4)

**4.23h**

Just a few final tweaks to the schematic and then the challenge of routing everything on the tiny board. ### 2026-11-08: The wonders of a good night's sleep can do to your project - in this case it makes you realise it was a bit flawed. A lot of this time was spent fixing the BOM and then realizing that all that work wa

**3.92h**

The wonders of a good night's sleep can do to your project - in this case it makes you realise it was a bit flawed. A lot of this time was spent fixing the BOM and then realizing that all that work was basically for not since JLC can't assemble boards so small  so in an act of desperation I have added sort of break off tabs  to stretch to board to the minimum size - also went down a small rabbit home of what the heck a fiducial mark is and how technically I need them for each IC but no way I can fit this so I let JLC take care of that for me I hope

[Timelapse](https://lookout.hackclub.com/api/media/7d34e732-7627-4dbb-83a7-e56e3d51c12c/video.mp4)

**2.75h**

Genuinely spent far too long trying to get JLC to actually assemble my boards - since I love to take shortcuts and so only made sure to use the same footprint instead of part in Fusion - so when I tried to then export the mechanical files I went insane trying to upload them again and again after it saying no can do. What did  it in the end was thing the sample files and manually putting in each component name, part number , location , rotation by hand which took me far too long. Also I dislike Microsoft excel with a passion so it was extra bad.
